messages:

Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing and budget — looking for flexibility

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loved the latency profile and the observability hooks. We have a constrained pilot budget for Q4 and a firm cap on unit spend. To make this work we need a deeper onboarding concession than your standard starter credit — looking at an effective 45% discount in year one across the first 12 months.

Attached is a short forecast for the pilot (includes expected tokens and projected monthly spend). If you can get close to this effective discount we can commit to a 12-month pilot with a conversion target and an option to expand into Dedicated in H2 next year.

Appreciate it,

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot pricing and budget — looking for flexibility

Folks — forwarding Alicia's ask from Soteria. Key ask: effective ~45% in year one across the pilot window. They can commit to 12 months and are motivated to convert.

My read: 45% is above our standard playbook and will materially affect margin unless we get a longer commit or an upfront. Proposal below (my suggested path) — need quick guidance on whether this qualifies for VP/CFO exception or if we should counter with a structured alternative to avoid the exception: 

Proposed commercial compromise (for internal discussion):
- Blended effective discount: 42% for months 1-12 (tiered usage breakpoints)
- Requirement: 12-month commitment with a minimum ARR floor of $1.2M and $200k upfront credit application (non-refundable onboarding credit)
- DocuSign for commitments and clear conversion KPIs (usage + success metrics)
- Contingent clause: if Soteria expands to Dedicated within 12 months, waive the onboarding credit offset by a 6-month bill-back schedule.

Why 42%? Moves them toward their ask while staying under the 45% legal threshold we've flagged historically for CFO signoff. Even at 42% the margin hit is non-trivial — I've attached a quick expected revenue profile. If we can't secure the upfront + ARR floor, recommend we decline the 45% ask and counter with a 30% concession + stronger success-based credits.

Please weigh in and flag if you want me to route to Marissa/VP for signoff. Time-sensitive — they want a formal answer by Thursday COB.

Thanks,
Hannah
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment: soteria_forecast_q4.xlsx (forwarded)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing and budget — looking for flexibility

Hannah — thanks for the summary. I ran a quick sensitivity on the raw unit economics. If they give $200k upfront and commit to the $1.2M floor, 42% is defendable short-term (we preserve visibility and optionality to upsell). If they only do 12 months with no upfront, 42% erases the majority of the margin and I'd push back.

Alternate path to avoid exec escalation: offer 33% off list pricing + a milestone-based rebate (spread over three months) tied to usage thresholds. That protects us and still reduces their cash outlay. Use the full 42% path only if Marissa signs off — this meets the >40% exception threshold that needs finance signoff.

Ben
VP, Commercial Strategy
ben.carter@redwood.com

Note: See attached margin summary for the 42% vs 33% scenarios. Attachment: margin_impact_summary.pdf (5 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Team — I've reviewed Ben's calculations and Hannah's ask. Key decision points: margin impact, churn risk, and whether the $200k upfront is enforceable. From a finance perspective, anything >40% effective concession on a new logo needs CFO visibility and VP-level alignment. I'll escalate to CFO for a one-time exception only if the following are locked in:

1) Signed DocuSign commitment with minimum ARR floor $1.2M
2) $200k non-refundable onboarding credit applied against the first invoice
3) Clear KPIs (monthly usage band and conversion criteria) with a clawback schedule if KPIs missed

If Soteria won't sign to those terms, approve the 33% + milestone rebate route. I can take the exception to CFO this afternoon if Ben confirms the 42% fallback and legal drafts the clause.

Marissa
Head of Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Alicia — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. I have an approved conditional offer we think balances your budget constraints and our commercial guardrails. Summary below: 

- One-time blended onboarding concession: effective 42% discount applied across the first 12 months (per attached schedule)
- Conditions: signed 12-month commitment with a minimum ARR floor of $1.2M and a $200k non-refundable onboarding credit applied to month 1 invoice
- KPIs: monthly usage band and two health-check milestones at month 3 and month 6 with success metrics to be included in the DocuSign exhibit
- If Soteria expands to Dedicated within the 12-month period, we will waive the onboarding credit and invoice on the Dedicated rate (subject to a 6-month bill-back schedule)

I've attached the formal proposal for signature. If you can sign the DocuSign by next Tuesday we will lock pricing and queue onboarding. If your procurement needs a lower cash outlay we can alternatively propose a 33% discount + milestone-based rebate (Ben's suggestion) — let me know which path you'd prefer and I'll route accordingly.
